rulings.finding: Choose shields first; trigger one before-break ability per break. Resolve all such abilities (choose/cast/finish each spell separately), then other waiting triggered abilities, then break selected shields.
Each spell selection uses current mana card count. First Boil Charger raising mana3→4 permits second cost4 spell.

Charger self-movement replacement takes mandatory priority over external deck-bottom replacement. Cyclepedia and Interstellar cases confirm 609.8a. Thus normal Charger, RSFK AllIn Charger and Crystal Charger should use own mana destination instead of Kaku bottom; no RSFK-specific Kaku QA found.

409.1/1b/1c: casting creates pending state, not a zone change. Card stays a member of original zone but is excluded from its count and cannot be used as another card. Only after resolution does it go to graveyard or replacement destination. Removing from internal source array for counts is reasonable but must not emit source-zone departure event.
Resolve selected modes in printed order. A creature deployed by first mode can receive speed/untap mode afterwards.
Chosen creature evolves via Invasion during attack: affected evolution creature untaps at attack end; same-creature effects inherited.
Granting during first attack works at its end. Official starter deck describes Karakuribaashi entry casting untap; official match report explicitly grants during Kaku before-break then untaps.

Text refers to that creature first attack this turn; 603.6a forbids retroactive delayed triggers. Grant after first attack has ended should not untap after a later attack. Evolution is same creature so previous-attack history should carry; Revolution Change is new zone entry so new creature history and does not inherit old creature grant. Direct exact-case QA not found.

Each delayed trigger instance is independent. Multiple grants before first attack end all trigger at that same end, not one untap reserved per later attack. 110.2c and 603.2/603.6 support this; exact repeated Fire QA not found.
Clock turn skip happens before attack-end step and prevents untap trigger.

Genmu ignores continuous effects AND delayed triggered abilities generated by cost5-or-lower spells, including already resolved spells. If Genmu leaves before trigger time, effect resumes. Applies to Fire and Peecap spell regardless cost of chosen creature.
